reason: Build-time and .NET-only: it EMITS source, so its contract is the shape of what it emits rather than a surface a browser calls. Its implementation uses StringBuilder and CultureInfo.InvariantCulture for the TypeScript backend, and its .fsproj Content-Removes the fable/ source distribution every other packable project ships — so it makes no portability promise for this gate to keep.

A dotnet TOOL (OutputType Exe, PackAsTool, command `fuaran-core-idl`): a .NET console entry point over the .NET-only generation half above. Like Idl.Codegen it Content-Removes the fable/ source distribution, so nothing it ships is Fable-compiled by a consumer either. It was packable and uncovered from Phase 127 until Phase 185 derived this list rather than remembering it.
